title: What Is Your Leadership Derailer
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece introduces personality psychologist Robert Hogan's framework of leadership 'derailers' -- the idea that poor leadership stems not from missing strengths but from an ordinary trait taken to an extreme. Using Excitability as an extended example, it shows how a generally positive quality (high energy, passion) can become a career-limiting liability when unmoderated, making a leader seem erratic or unable to be taken seriously. The essay lists several other derailers from Hogan's research (skepticism, cautiousness, imagination, among others) and extends the list with additional candidates, closing with the practical advice that everyone has at least one derailer and the goal is awareness and moderation, not denial.
points: Robert Hogan's core insight: poor leadership usually comes from an excess of an ordinary trait, not the absence of some needed quality.
Excitability illustrates the pattern -- high energy and passion are assets until taken to an extreme, where they undermine a leader's credibility.
Hogan and colleagues identify roughly ten common derailers, including skepticism, cautiousness, mischievousness, colorfulness, diligence, and imagination.
Additional plausible derailers include arrogance, close-mindedness, perfectionism, impulsiveness, passive-aggressiveness, and dominance.
The practical advice is not to deny having a derailer but to identify it and work to moderate, offset, or tether its effects.
quotes: Poor leadership is not about lacking some essential quality, but rather it is the excess of an undesirable one.
Leaders are derailed by their profound weaknesses more than by missing strengths.
While their excitability can inspire and motivate others to action, if taken to an extreme, it can derail a leader's ability to be taken seriously.
Like many other personality traits, Excitability can be a friend or a foe for a leader.
Nearly any predisposition or personality trait when taken to extreme can derail the long-term success of a leader.
Remember, a leadership derailer is never just a weakness. It is simply a personality extreme that requires improvement for any leader to realize their full potential.
